summary: This paper proves sharp structural lower bounds and compression across all three stages of the Fotakis et al. (2026) PSPACE-completeness reduction for Pinwheel Scheduling. In Stage 1, it proves strip high hour H=5, inter-region gap g=3, and a 4-day write phase are exact minimums, compressing width from 72N+15 to 60N+13 and calendar period from 8m+32 to 8m+8. In Stage 2, it proves any two-hour coprimality witness gadget of arbitrary size r (allowing prime powers) with chi(G)>=3 and omega(G)<=2 contains an induced odd cycle C_{2s+1} (s>=2) whose non-edges require at least 5 distinct primes, forcing K>=2310 unconditionally; at K=2310 on C_5, (6,10,55,77,21) with CRT phases (4,5,11,56,15) uniquely minimizes rigid fillers at 3822 (saving 180 per test vs. 4002). In Stage 3, it sharpens density slack and expected deviation from n*Delta to the moving-job rate S_2 and proves a per-job total-variation cut theorem tightening the soundness day-length threshold from T > n(2E+3) to the single-slot-exact bound T >= E+1 (saving >2n in the cut step and Omega(n^2/w_mov) overall). Eighteen core algebraic/combinatorial theorems are proved in constructive Lean 4.35.0 (zero sorry, zero Classical.choice) alongside 16 zero-float SHA-256 certificates.
strengths: Universal combinatorial number-theoretic lower bound (Theorem 2a) via induced odd cycles and independent-set non-edge counting, proving K >= 2310 across all graphs with chi(G) >= 3 and omega(G) <= 2 even with arbitrary prime powers.

Exact per-job total-variation cut theorem (Theorem 3b-c) improving Stage-3 soundness day-length threshold from T > n(2E+3) to T >= E+1 (Omega(n^2/w_mov) overall) with a matching single-slot tightness construction at E=T.
Tight, constructive Stage-1 compression (Theorem 1) cutting width to 60N+13 and write-phase overhead by 75% (M=8m+8) with explicit counterexamples at H=4, g=2, and L<=3.

Exemplary formalization and reproducibility: all 18 core algebraic/combinatorial theorems compile in constructive Lean 4.35.0 using only [propext, Quot.sound], supported by a zero-float Python verifier and SHA-256 manifest.
weaknesses: Optimizes and characterizes exact constants within the three-stage Fotakis et al. (2026) reduction framework rather than introducing a new complexity-theoretic paradigm or improving worst-case PSPACE hardness.

Lean 4.35.0 formalization verifies the 18 core algebraic/combinatorial lemmas rather than mechanizing the full end-to-end reduction equivalence from Periodic 3-SAT, and the introduction briefly overloads Omega as both asymptotic notation and the window-length parameter.
